items.title: Karl-Anthony Towns, Knicks 'Tens Of Millions Apart' On Extension
items.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns and the New York Knicks are currently significantly apart on their positions as they discuss a contract extension. Towns can sign for up to $276 million over four years on an extension and is not believed to be demanding the max in talks with the Knicks. If Towns and the Knicks are unable to agree to an extension, he could decline his $61 million player option to become a free agent. Towns could alternatively exercise his option at that amount, which would almost certainly put the Knicks into the second apron for the 2027-28 season. "I want to talk about the overall value of the contract, because Karl-Anthony Towns is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension," said Brian Windhorst on Friday's Hoop Collective Podcast. "That's his max that he's eligible to get. He obviously has... he and his side have a position on what he wants to sign for. The Knicks have a position on what they have offered. So those are the parameters. From what I understand, they are tens of millions apart. They're not close," said "Honestly, I believe that they could be eight figures apart on an annual basis," said Tim MacMahon. "I believe that's-you know, and maybe it's changed since we've been starting this podcast, maybe the offers have changed," replied Windhorst. "But again, KAT is not pounding the table and saying, 'You've got to max me.' He's willing to have discussions," said MacMahon. "Oh, yeah. He's willing to take less than the $275 million, I believe," said Windhorst. "The question, you know, the question is what are the Knicks willing to do?" Towns is represented by Jessica Holtz of CAA, which is the former agency of Leon Rose. CAA also represents Jalen Brunson, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart.

items.title: Jalen Brunson 'Fully Cleared' From Offseason Wrist Surgery
items.summary: New York Knicks fans can breathe a sigh of relief with training camp set to open next week. Star guard Jalen Brunson told fans that he's "fully recovered" from offseason surgery on his left wrist. "As you guys know, I had surgery this offseason," Brunson told the crowd at a live taping of the "Roomates Show" with teammate Josh Hart. "And I just wanted to tell you guys that I am fully cleared." Brunson had previously said that he suffered the wrist injury during Game 2 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Cleveland Cavaliers. He held off on surgery to help lead the Knicks to the NBA Finals and ultimately the 2026 title.

items.title: Kevin Knox, Magic Sign Training Camp Contract
items.summary: The Orlando Magic signed forward Kevin Knox II to a training camp contract. Knox is likely to land with the Osceola Magic for the G League season, as Orlando is likely to keep their final roster spot open into the season. Knox spent last season with the Windy City Bulls of the G League. The seven-year NBA veteran averaged 21.4 points and 7.6 points in 39 games. Knox last played in the NBA with the Golden State Warriors in 2024-25 season. The 6-foot-8 forward has also played for the New York Knicks, Atlanta Hawks, Portland Trail Blazers and Detroit Pistons in the NBA.

items.title: Karl-Anthony Towns, Knicks Unlikely To Sign Extension Before Start Of Camp
items.summary: Karl-Anthony Towns and the New York Knicks have "stagnated" on their contract extension discussions and a deal before the start of training camp is considered unlikely. Despite the lack of progress, the talks have been described as "cordial." Towns has been eligible for a contract extension during the offseason that could reach $276 million over four seasons. "This is a cloud going into training camp," said Shams Charania. Towns has a $61 million player option for the 2027-28 season and could become a free agent in 2027. There is no deadline for an extension between Towns and the Knicks. Towns will turn 31 in November. James Dolan has been clear that he wants to avoid the Knicks going into the second apron.
